description: What exists in Schnabelglück (Phaser + Matter edition), which design principles were decided, and the contracts a new stage or obstacle must satisfy. Every entity points at the code that implements it; properties.constants mirror exported constants exactly and properties.telegraph is simulated; tests/design.test.js validates this file and cross-checks it against src/.

concepts.description: A creature or person drawn as an individual in the sea world.
The player character, steered with a single hold/release control.
Something the hero can do with hold (dive) and release (fly), or taps while airborne.
A resource or rule that shapes every run (energy, air, cargo, pace).
Something in Pip's way that he must read and avoid or handle; every obstacle declares how it is telegraphed (properties.telegraph).
An obstacle whose contact hurts: it ends the run, costs energy, or (terrain) bounces Pip and costs energy.
Contact ends the run at once.
Contact costs energy (contactDamage) once and gives brief protection; it never takes cargo or air.
A force on Pip and fish (flowAt) without any contact rule; it cannot hurt, only drag Pip off course.
Solid scenery in Matter: Pip bounces off and loses energy and speed instead of ending the run.
A harmless animal that shares the water with Pip.
An authored combination entry in a stage's encounter list (kinds joined by '-').
Something that pays points, energy or air.
An item Pip catches or touches.
A kind of fish (src/species.js): how often it appears per stage, how far and fast it dodges Pip, and its base points; drawn by src/fishes.js.
Points for a skilful action or a streak.
Spectacle rolled per run between the regular encounters (rollSetPieces).
An optional reward placed only on calm 'turtle-turtle-gull' waves.
Scenery only; no gameplay effect.
One special moment per run and stage, at a random wave in the middle (rollRare).
A weather element of the storm stage.
One nest of the journey; order is progression and save index.
What a stage is played towards.
Background decor animal or object, scattered differently every run (rollDecor).
A user-interface screen, dialog or overlay outside the canvas world.
Data and rules a new stage or obstacle must satisfy; each is checked by tests/design.test.js.
Why a run ended (game.endReason); shown as the result title via reasons.<id>.
An event returned by step() (GameEvent typedef); presentation reacts to it with sound, haptics, juice and labels.
Music or ambience mixed by audio.js.
An accessibility property of the game as built.
A cosmetic look for Pip drawn by pelican(): one head accessory (saved as outfit), combinable with the Hawaiian shirt.

A preset colour set for Pip's feathers, beak or Hawaiian shirt (src/looks.js), chosen in the wardrobe and saved on the device; presets instead of a free picker keep Pip readable against sky and water.

rules.statement: Every obstacle is telegraphed before it can hurt. 'Telegraphed' means the player gets at least one announcement — a warning event (with the shared warning sound, plus the shark's jittering warn pose, the diver's aim line, the boat's wind-up), a harmless visible state change (puffer startles and inflates, the great white shows only its fin), or, for static obstacles, being visible from the right screen edge — at least properties.telegraph.leadSeconds before it can first hurt or pull Pip.

check.name: sharks track faster later, telegraph a fixed dash, and stop pursuing above water
diver locks aim before firing, reloads, and missed harpoons award only once
fishermen announce a fixed cast, splash once and retrieve their visible net
puffer gives a full second of anticipation and is dangerous only when puffed
every obstacle is telegraphed with its declared lead time
check.gap: Lead times are simulated at reef pace with Pip held at one depth per obstacle; other speeds and player paths are not simulated.

rules.statement: Each danger first appears alone before it appears in a combination, across the whole journey.

check.name: the journey introduces dangers before combining them and has activity in every encounter
authored stages introduce individual dangers before combinations and finish safely

rules.statement: Shark bites are fatal, but there is always an escape (surfacing or a free band; for the great white the shallow fish trail); shark pairs leave a free band and never more than two sharks overlap.

check.name: sharks, fishermen and divers end the stage while other creatures only drain energy
every shark pair leaves a reachable band after a visible reaction delay
encounter traces do not repeat and never overlap more than two sharks
surfacing shakes off the great white without a bite
the great white cannot reach the fish trail just under the surface
a steady depth outswims the great white; bobbing up and down gets caught
jumping out makes the great white sweep across and scatter the creatures
